name: Hot Springs
intro: Hot Springs is the destination-wedding town of Arkansas, and it earns it. Couples don't just book a venue here — they plan a weekend: the lake, the Ouachitas, historic Bathhouse Row downtown, and at the center of it all, Garvan Woodland Gardens, where I filmed a wedding beneath the glass canopy of Anthony Chapel. That chapel is one of the most iconic ceremony spaces in the state, and the 210 acres of gardens around it — bridges, waterfalls, Lake Hamilton at the edge — give a film a setting that feels more like a fairy tale than a Saturday.

Filming in Hot Springs means knowing the rhythms of a destination day: guests arriving from out of town, tighter ceremony windows at the popular venues, and light that changes fast between the mountains and the lake. I've made that drive from Little Rock plenty of times, and it's one I never mind — few places in Arkansas hand a videographer this much beauty to work with.

faqs.question: Do you travel to Hot Springs?
faqs.answer: Yes, all the time — it's about an hour from my base in Little Rock. Travel is included within 50 miles of Little Rock, and Hot Springs sits right around that edge, so depending on your exact venue there's either no fee or a small one at $1 per mile past 50. You'll see the exact number in your quote — never a surprise.

faqs.question: How far in advance should we book?
faqs.answer: Hot Springs venues — Anthony Chapel especially — book far in advance, so nine to twelve months out is the safe window. I take one wedding per date; a retainer locks yours in.

faqs.question: When will we get our films?
faqs.answer: Your Instagram reel arrives within 48 hours — perfect for the post-wedding-weekend glow. Your full film is delivered by a guaranteed date, in writing.
